content_voiceover: This slide walks through how we actually treat classical Hodgkin lymphoma, and the key concept is that therapy is both risk-adjusted and response-adapted. Risk-adjusted means we ask up front whether disease is unfavorable or bulky, which sets the starting regimen. Response-adapted means we use interim FDG-PET imaging mid-treatment to escalate or de-escalate therapy, and the pivotal trial here is RATHL, response-adapted therapy in Hodgkin lymphoma. In RATHL, over 1200 newly diagnosed patients got two cycles of ABVD, then an interim PET scan. PET-negative patients continued on ABVD or dropped the bleomycin to AVD, while PET-positive patients escalated to intensified BEACOPP. Three-year progression-free survival was 85 percent with ABVD or AVD versus 68 percent with escalated BEACOPP in the PET-positive group, which tells you PET positivity itself is a marker of higher-risk biology. By stage and risk group: favorable stage I-II gets three cycles of ABVD; unfavorable non-bulky stage I-II gets two cycles of ABVD followed by four of AVD; unfavorable bulky stage I-II adds involved-site radiotherapy, ISRT, after the same chemo backbone. Advanced stage III-IV historically got six cycles of ABVD plus ISRT, but the modern NCCN preferred regimens have shifted toward novel combinations: nivolumab-AVD, BrECADD, and brentuximab vedotin-AVD, all built to reduce bleomycin-related pulmonary toxicity while improving outcomes.
keypoints: RATHL: ABVD x2 -> PET; PET- continue ABVD/AVD, PET+ escalate to BEACOPP
Stage I-II: ABVD(3) favorable; ABVD/AVD +/- ISRT if unfavorable/bulky
Stage III-IV: newer options replacing bleomycin - Nivo-AVD, BrECADD, BV-AVD
keypoint_voiceover: Two concepts drive Hodgkin treatment: risk-adjusted therapy based on unfavorable or bulky features at diagnosis, and response-adapted therapy guided by interim PET, as shown in the RATHL trial, where PET-negative patients stayed on ABVD or AVD with 85 percent 3-year PFS, while PET-positive patients needed escalated BEACOPP. For advanced stage III and IV disease, remember the newer bleomycin-sparing regimens replacing classic ABVD: nivolumab-AVD, BrECADD, and brentuximab vedotin-AVD.
